Docs/Styling

Styling

This page goes over how to style your pages in Elegance.

CSS Object

Element's support style={} objects, just as is normal in JSX.

You can use them like this:

tsx
<button
    style={{
        backgroundColor: "black",
    }}
>
</button>

Obviously these also work in function-style:

ts
button({
    style: {
        backgroundColor: "black";
    }
});

CSS Files

If you're slightly more sane, you'll want .css files to write your styles in. The easiest way to write these is to put them in your public/ directory, but for a more robust approach, you can put them in your pages/ directory, and use our build hooks to publish them.

CSS Frameworks

If you'd like to use something like tailwind, postcss, sass, etc; those are all very much usable in Elegance.

Sass / SCSS

npm i sass

ts
import sass from "sass";
import { dirname } from "node:path";

export const config: EleganceConfig = {
    css: {
        transformers: [
            {
                test: /\.(scss|sass)$/,
                transform: (source, file) =>
                    sass.compileString(source, {
                        loadPaths: [dirname(file), "node_modules"],
                        // .sass uses the indented syntax — must be explicit
                        syntax: file.endsWith(".sass") ? "indented" : "scss",
                    }).css,
            },
        ],
    },
};

Less

npm i less

ts
import less from "less";
import { dirname } from "node:path";

{
    test: /\.less$/,
    transform: (source, file) =>
        less.render(source, {
            paths: [dirname(file), "node_modules"],
            filename: file,
        }).then((out) => out.css),
}

Stylus

npm i stylus

ts
import stylus from "stylus";
import { dirname } from "node:path";

{
    test: /\.styl(us)?$/,
    transform: (source, file) =>
        new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
            stylus(source)
                .set("filename", file)
                .set("paths", [dirname(file)])
                .render((err, css) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve(css)));
        }),
}

PostCSS (autoprefixer, nesting, etc.)

PostCSS's JS API does not auto-load postcss.config.js — pass plugins directly:

npm i postcss autoprefixer postcss-nested

ts
import postcss from "postcss";
import autoprefixer from "autoprefixer";
import postcssNested from "postcss-nested";

{
    test: /\.(css|pcss|postcss)$/,
    transform: (source, file) =>
        postcss([postcssNested(), autoprefixer()])
            .process(source, { from: file })
            .then((r) => r.css),
}

Tailwind v4

The official path is its PostCSS plugin (@tailwindcss/postcss handles @import "tailwindcss" and source detection itself; from drives its base directory):

npm i tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss

You'll need this somewhere in a css file.

css
@import "tailwindcss";

Add this to your css transformers:

ts
import postcss from "postcss";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/postcss";

{
    test: /\.css$/,
    transform: (source, file) =>
        postcss([tailwindcss()])
            .process(source, { from: file })
            .then((r) => r.css),
}

Tailwind v3 (needs content config)

npm i tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixer

ts
import postcss from "postcss";
import tailwindcss from "tailwindcss";
import autoprefixer from "autoprefixer";

{
    test: /\.(css|pcss|postcss)$/,
    transform: (source, file) =>
        postcss([tailwindcss(), autoprefixer()])
            .process(source, { from: file })
            .then((r) => r.css),
}
ts
export default { 
    /* ... */ 
    content: ["./pages/**/*.{tsx,ts}"], 
    /* ... */ 
};

Chaining multiple processors

Transformer order matters. To run Sass first, then autoprefix everything (including compiled output), the post-process step must match the original file paths too:

ts
transformers: [
    { test: /\.(scss|sass)$/, transform: sassTransform },
    { test: /\.less$/, transform: lessTransform },

    {
        test: /\.(css|scss|sass|less|styl|stylus|pcss|postcss)$/,
        transform: (source, file) =>
            postcss([autoprefixer()]).process(source, { from: file }).then((r) => r.css),
    },
]
